descriptors.R: nominee of the party out of the presidency since 1933
descriptors.D: nominee of the party in office since 1933; the sitting President is not running again

compile_desc.R: the party out of the presidency since 1933

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Progressive and a Prohibition nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Eisenhower, Stevenson, Nixon, Sparkman, Truman, Taft, Kefauver, MacArthur, McCarthy, Hallinan or Franklin Roosevelt

slice_sources.men: 1950 census aged to November 1952 along each group's 1940→1950 trend; men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only; Black voters here vote heavily Democratic since 1936; calibrated to certified 1952 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1950 census aged to November 1952, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1952 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1950 census aged to November 1952, white adults in the eleven former Confederate states, 18+ in Georgia; poll taxes remain only in Alabama, Arkansas, Mississippi, Texas and Virginia; calibrated to certified 1952 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1950 census aged to November 1952, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states (18+ in Georgia); registration keeps rising after the white primary's fall, but poll taxes, literacy tests and intimidation keep most disfranchised, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1950 census aged to November 1952, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; no state let aliens vote (the 1952 immigration act ending racial bars to naturalization takes effect after the election).
